missed_or_uncertain: What the file actually contains, so an adjudicator can decide whether the COMPROP memo belongs in the corpus under its own record (and to avoid re-reading it): design - Covid-related YouTube links were harvested from Facebook and Reddit via CrowdTangle (1 Oct 2019 - 30 Jun 2020) and from an open-access Twitter keyword dataset (Oct 2019 - Apr 2020, 268 keywords reduced to 71), giving 1,091,876 distinct YouTube videos; each link was followed and the removal reason recorded, identifying 8,105 Covid-related videos removed by YouTube for breaching its Community Guidelines, treated as 'Covid-related misinformation' on YouTube's own judgement; metadata recovered from the Wayback Machine for 935 videos (view counts) and 420 (visibility duration). Potentially extractable values if that record is created: (a) CONTENT-type prevalence - 8,105 removed misinformation videos out of the 1,091,876 distinct Covid-related YouTube videos found on social media, described in the summary as 'less than 1% of all YouTube videos about the coronavirus' (0.74% if computed, which R8 would not allow as a kept value since the memo states only 'less than 1%'); (b) CONCENTRATION, user/source dimension, with both halves stated - 'Just 250 communities have provided the same amount of visibility, in terms of shares, to misinformation than all the remaining communities combined' out of 32,607 distinct Facebook communities that posted links (250/32,607 = 0.77% of communities for ~50% of shares), and 'These three videos alone gathered 40% of the shares, comments and reactions given to all of the misinformation videos in our dataset' (3 of 8,105 videos); (c) platform-moderation coverage - 'Out of the 8,105 misinformation videos, only 55 had warning labels attached to them when we undertook our data collection; less than 1% of all the misinformation videos'; (d) intensity figures - videos were visible on average 41 days (n=420) and gathered on average 149,825 views before removal (n=935), shared on average 2,427 times on Facebook, 63 retweets on Twitter, 955 Reddit posts in total; 20 million shares and 71 million reactions/comments across Facebook, Twitter and Reddit versus 15 million shares for the five largest English-language news broadcasters on YouTube; 15 YouTube views per Facebook share, Facebook-shares/YouTube-views correlation 0.70 vs subscriber-count correlation 0.12; 89 copies of Plandemic; of 250 top communities, 91 English-language, of which conspiracy-related 27 and political 25, conspiracy communities posting on average 119 distinct videos with on average 51,006 followers. Caveats attaching to all of these: the misinformation label is YouTube's removal decision (removals can be for nudity or harassment too, as the memo itself notes), CrowdTangle covers only public pages/groups of significant size, and the Wayback subset is biased toward widely shared videos. Note that this document is a data memo that has explicitly NOT been peer reviewed.
